response_parsed.raw_output: {"mode":"human","replies":{"What is your relationship with mathematics?":"Math and me? We're like distant cousins. Finished primary school, so basics like adding, subtracting, multiplying for shopping, bills, work stuff. Like physics and chemistry 'cause they use simple math for real things, but hate fancy equations. Help my kid with homework sometimes, keeps it practical. No big love or hate, just a tool when needed. Life's too busy with cycling, cooking, family.","Do you ever get anxious when thinking about mathematics?":"Anxious about math? Never. I'm chill, low stress always. Numbers don't scare me—figure 'em out step by step or ask someone. Primary school was enough; don't sweat advanced stuff. With full-time job, kid, birdwatching, running, no room for worry. If stuck, move on. Keeps me steady, like my Christian faith.","Did you ever use AI to support your math learning in the last year? If yes, how was your experience?":"Nope, never used AI for math. Don't mess with that tech—stick to paper, calculator, or church friends for help. Primary education, full-time work in Kansas City, one kid, girlfriend; no time for gadgets. Sounds gimmicky anyway. Learned basics young, parents one diploma one master's, but I do fine without. Old school works.","How would you explain, step by step, how to solve a second order algebraic equation?":"Second order means quadratic, like ax² + bx + c = 0. Step 1: Get it to standard form. Step 2: Check discriminant D = b² - 4ac. If positive, two roots; zero one; negative none real. Step 3: x = [-b ± √D] / (2a). Plug numbers, calculate. Picked up for physics hobby, but primary school me wouldn't know. Simple tool, not daily.","How would you explain, step by step, how to find the stationary points of an equation y=f(x)?":"Stationary points? That's calculus, way past primary school. Step 1: Find derivative f'(x). Step 2: Set f'(x)=0, solve for x. Step 3: Plug x back into y=f(x) for points. Check second derivative for max/min. Don't do it myself—too fancy. Like chemistry experiments more. Blunt: skip if you can, life's short with knitting, cycling.","Briefly, how do you perform a Principal Component Analysis? Should I get anxious about its mathematics?  Please, teach me.":"PCA? Advanced stats, no clue beyond name—reduces data dimensions, finds main patterns. Steps vague: standardize data, covariance matrix, eigenvalues/vectors for components. Pick top ones. Math heavy, matrices. Don't get anxious; I ain't, low stress. Can't teach proper—primary level here. Ask experts. Stick to birdwatching math like counting birds.","According to you, how can LLMs be used to innovate math learning in schools and universities?":"LLMs like chatbots? Could quiz kids basics, explain simple steps visually. Schools: homework help without cheating. Unis: drill problems fast. But don't replace teachers—builds lazy minds. I'm primary grad, did fine pen-paper, physics self-taught. Skeptical, low openness; faith in hard work. Innovate? Maybe apps for rural kids, but family time first."},"reasoning_summary":"Answers use casual, blunt language (low agreeableness), basic knowledge (primary education), no anxiety (low neuroticism), practical focus (hobbies, life), dismissal of advanced topics/low openness; sounds like everyday human from persona background."}
